newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas falls again, trades heavily before close.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas falls again, trades heavily before close.

text.p: The IPE natural gas contract saw a large volume of trade one minute before the market closed on Monday afternoon, with every month from March to August traded at that time.
Prices were once again sharply off, with March closing 1.30 pence a therm below Friday's settlement level.
"It looks as if it was a strip," said a broker, adding that it was hard to pinpoint exactly what had happened.
The total volume of 260 lots traded was considered "respectable" by brokers, and there was some surprise by the further fall in the value of March.

"March will just be got out of the way. People aren't too interested in taking delivery," said a broker, although he pointed out that the fall in serious March interest comes a full 10 days before the contract closes on February 27.

There was continued good interest for back months, and the last two trades in every month from April to August were done at 10 pence a therm, confirming the trend seen on Friday for the summer to talk in an extremely flat range.

"The backs had been overvalued and they're now dropping down," said a broker. But March remains the contract traded in the widest range, falling by 5.70 pence a therm from a contract high of 14.90 pence to 9.20 pence immediately before Monday's close.
